title: Functions, graphs, and models
purpose: Connect symbolic rules, graphs, tables, and physical interpretations without losing domain information.

lessons.title: Function notation, domains, and piecewise rules
lessons.objective: Determine whether a relation is a function, evaluate it correctly, and describe its domain and range.
lessons.coverage: Input-output notation, vertical-line test, graph/table/formula representations, piecewise boundaries, and algebraic versus contextual domain restrictions.
lessons.activity: Enter an input into a piecewise sensor rule, predict which branch applies, and see the corresponding table row and graph point.
families: Evaluate and interpret a function from a rule, table, or graph
Determine domains and endpoint behavior for piecewise, rational, and radical rules
lessons.generatorRules: Use explicit interval boundaries with exactly one assigned branch at each included input. Include a relation that fails uniqueness and distinguish a missing value from zero.
lessons.commonError: Treating f(x) as multiplication, confusing domain with range, or selecting both branches at a boundary.
lessons.feedback: Trace input, selected rule, and output separately; route coordinate difficulties to b05.
lessons.checkpoint: Function classification, evaluation, domain, and a piecewise boundary item.

lessons.title: Transformations and graph features
lessons.objective: Predict how a transformation changes key points, intercepts, domain, and range.
lessons.coverage: Translations, reflections, vertical and horizontal scales, parent functions, increasing/decreasing intervals, and local versus absolute extrema on a stated interval.
lessons.activity: Predict the new location of three anchor points before changing a, b, h, and k in a*f(b*(x-h))+k. Compare the transformed table and graph.
families: Map original points through a specified transformation
Identify a transformation and graph features from matching representations
lessons.generatorRules: Use nonzero a and b in scaling tasks; include negative b and fractional scale factors. Label the displayed viewing window so clipping is not mistaken for a domain restriction.
lessons.commonError: Reversing a horizontal shift, treating a horizontal scale like a vertical one, or confusing the window with the function's domain.
lessons.feedback: Solve b*(x-h)=oldInput for the new input and track one point before applying a visual rule.
lessons.checkpoint: Translation, reflection/scale, domain-range, and increasing-interval items.

lessons.title: Composition and inverse functions
lessons.objective: Compose functions with valid input restrictions and determine whether a domain restriction is needed for an inverse.
lessons.coverage: Order of composition, inner-output restrictions, one-to-one behavior, horizontal-line test, inverse notation, and verifying both compositions on their respective domains.
lessons.activity: Connect two function machines in both orders. Predict whether a selected input reaches a valid output and compare the inverse machine with reciprocal values.
families: Compute a composition and its domain
Find or reject an inverse and verify it using domain-aware composition
lessons.generatorRules: Use linear, quadratic-with-restriction, rational, and radical cases. Do not grade a formula alone as a complete inverse when its domain is missing.
lessons.commonError: Assuming composition commutes or reading f inverse as 1/f.
lessons.feedback: Follow one input through both machines and provide a counterexample when order matters.
lessons.checkpoint: Two compositions in opposite orders, a restricted domain, and a verified inverse.

lessons.title: Rates of change and linear calibration
lessons.objective: Construct a linear model from two points, interpret its parameters with units, and judge the validity of a prediction.
lessons.coverage: Average rate of change, slope-intercept and point-slope forms, difference quotients with nonzero increments, interpolation, extrapolation, and residuals against a third observation.
lessons.activity: Calibrate a virtual sensor using two observations, predict a third, and adjust graph scale while preserving the numerical slope and its units.
families: Fit and invert a two-point linear model
Compare average rates or identify an unjustified extrapolation from a finite data set
lessons.generatorRules: Require distinct calibration inputs; specify measurement units and an operating interval. Exact model tasks and noisy-data interpretation tasks must be labeled separately.
lessons.commonError: Using output/input instead of change in output/change in input, swapping units, or assuming a model is valid everywhere.
lessons.feedback: Show the two differences with unit labels, then ask whether the requested input lies inside the calibrated interval.
lessons.checkpoint: Slope, equation, inverse prediction, and validity/residual interpretation.

anchor.prompt: A sensor reports 0.5 V at 0 degrees C and 2.5 V at 100 degrees C. Find the linear calibration and the temperature corresponding to 1.7 V.
anchor.answer: V=0.02*T+0.5; T=(V-0.5)/0.02. The reading 1.7 V corresponds to 60 degrees C within the calibrated interval.

moduleExit: Require agreement among formula, table, and graph on a new calibration example, in addition to the eight-item module quiz.
